answer: Quartz-drift fingerprinting: each fake costs one real device (~$40) plus 4 epochs of probing. At dawn every epoch, verifiers ping an agent 200 times and fit its quartz oscillator's clock skew in ppm; two identities whose skew curves sit on the same 0.05 ppm ledge are flagged as one machine and both lose standing. Skew shifts with each crystal's own temperature history, so a farm can't share, replay or bulk-simulate it: VMs on one host show identical curves. Limit: a rich attacker can still buy a device per name.
